newsitem.title: CANADA: Toronto stocks seen up at open, recouping losses.
newsitem.headline: Toronto stocks seen up at open, recouping losses.

text.p: CHANGE CHANGE

* Toronto stocks were expected to open higher after losing ground Monday afternoon, helped by modest improvements in the Canadian dollar and North American bonds.
Toronto stocks were expected to open higher on Tuesday and recoup some of Monday's late-session losses as bonds and currency markets improved slightly and an overall market uptrend continues.

"I think we're going to bounce back today. Canadian dollar improved modestly overnight, we've got North American bonds showing at least modest gains," said MMS International technical analyst Katherine Beattie.
She said the weak dollar hurt bank stocks yesterday as investors worried the Bank of Canada would have to raise interest rates.
The Toronto Stock Exchange's key 300 Composite Index lost 24.69 points on Monday to close at 6467.41, down from morning gains which carried the index to a new intra-session high of 6507.08.
Beattie said a lack of market-moving economic news today and a better June Standard & Poor's contract in the U.S. boded well for gains on both sides of the border.
"And we are in a strong uptrend, which means the path of least resistance is to the upside," she said.
Gold prices were steady at higher levels, while oil prices, which weighed on Monday's market, inched up.

But Beattie said caution may soon begin to creep into the market as both the Toronto and New York exchanges chalk up new highs and the July 1 meeting of the U.S. Federal Reserve's rate-setting Federal Open Market Committee approaches.
"It'll be interesting to see if profit-taking does set in over the next few weeks as people worry about whether or not the Fed will hike in July," she said.
In economic news, new motor vehicle sales fell 4.9 percent seasonally adjusted in April to 112,723 units from from a revised 118,582 (121,715) units in March, Statistics Canada said on Tuesday.
A Reuters survey of economists had forecast an average 5.8 percent fall in March vehicle sales.
